reason: The narrative demonstrates the opposite of this statement. King Saul, the leader, is portrayed as unjustly pursuing David with intent to kill him. David is innocent and wronged. Jonathan, despite being the king's son, repeatedly defends David and questions his father's actions, saying 'Why should he be put to death? What has he done?' (וַיֹּ֧אמֶר אֵלָ֛יו לָ֥מָּה יוּמַ֖ת מֶ֥ה עָשָֽׂה). Saul grows angry and even attempts to strike Jonathan with a spear in his rage. The text clearly portrays the leader (Saul) as wrong and the protagonist (David) and his ally (Jonathan) as righteous and justified.
